I'm sure the multiplayer is great, for those who enjoy playing their games with random adolescents from the internet, but it baffles me when I have to devote time to logging into an online server to play completely solo. To make sure that I hold this against the game, it does it when you try to exit out of the game too. "Sure, hold on three minutes, while I log back into the gosh darn online server, just so you can tell me you want to quit playing one more time. You'll of course have a few minutes wait for it to close out from there too. Please enjoy this loading icon!" I just ctr+alt+dlt, when I want to quit out of the game. I hope it corrupts their data a little. The game play is fine. I guess they really wanted to be Dark Souls and Gears of War at the same time. They largely succeeded. Take that how you will. It seems a little forced and lacking some fine tuning, imo. Of course, I'm bad at games, so form your own opinion about that part.

Casual Warhammer fan, played the Total War games and then tried 40k with some friends, loved the Chaos Daemons and didn't care for many others, Space Marines are now cool. 

The game isn't complex, it is a fun shooter cut through lots of enemies, feel like a badass, carry on. 

All modes in this game are fun, I LOVED the campaign and I've not played a campaign in a game (That isn't an RPG) since maybe 10+ years ago? I worried it would get boring towards the middle or end but no it kept my interest and despite never touching Space Marine 1, I still felt like I could just jump in where I was and not feel lost but I'm sure there's a fair bit of context I missed because of it which I will now be going online to find.

PvP is fun, better balanced than most games, you need your team you can't just solo everything or run and gun everyone, the generally "Stronger" classes are hard countered by others, the devs are ironing things out still and are responding well to feedback.

The Operations mode is amazing, I actually played this before the campaign with a friend because I just didn't think I'd want to play the Campaign and ended up doing it afterwards anyway, loved it, the Operations mode you play as another squad at different sections of the battlefield that were in the campaign, but in the campaign you get to see the effects of that squad's actions. I'm really excited to see where the game goes.

Expensive? Yes, but this game feels like it's going to a good core of gaming and I don't know if it's just me but it feels like what gaming used to feel like.

With how AAA titles have been launching recently, WH40k Space Marine 2 is a breath of fresh air.  Launched fine, no crazy graphical bugs or issues, all game modes worked, partying up is easy, and it feels like they did a completely thorough polishing then polished it again.  
There are some nitpicks but its just my opinion as a fan.  There is no Power Axe, equipable flamer, no Lightning claws or chain fist.  You dont see any ogryn, zealot types, psychers except for campaign, or terminators!!  I think (i know I could be compltely wrong on this) that Titus joins the 2nd company of Ultramarines and not a single terminator in sight.  not even armor on a table under maintenance or something.
Also the executions get repetative, and theres not enough weapon specific kill animations.  Most of the time your just tearing a an body part off with your bare hands.  which is cool, but like, the potential for awesome execution animations is crazy high.

Not worth $79.99 should be around $39.99 even after all the roadmap content is delivered. The gameplay is generic, clunky, and full of glitches. You compete for class selection because only one class can be used on a team at a time. Melee classes absolutely fall short because they don't have primary weapons and can't use they're abilities on zoanthropes leaving your team at a complete disadvantage. Weapons don't damage enemies remotely close to what they should based on the 40k stats which hinders the experience. The Grapnel launcher is incredibly buggy. 

Overall, it's been a mediocre experience and I hope it improves. When it gets better I'll definitely change this to a positive review. I would recommend waiting a year for it to go on sale and is polished to a much finer state.

[[Review written at game launch, does not account for post-launch content updates]]
One of my top games for 2024. The three modes of play: Campaign (Solo), Operations (PvE), and Eternal War (PvP) are all incredibly fun.

In Operations, class progression is fast enough to feel meaningful, but slow enough that you can take the time to enjoy lower-level gameplay and ease yourself into the more difficult content.

In Eternal War, the maps are small enough that you will spend most of the match engaging with enemy players, even if you die a lot like I do. Firearms are pretty powerful, but there's a good chance you'll be engaging in melee combat too (it's almost guaranteed if you play certain classes.) As a very casual player, I was pleasantly surprised to find out I was enjoying PvP.
--
Complaints... 
The Jump-Pack wargear functions differently in the Campaign, Operations, and Eternal War modes. I found it was most enjoyable in Eternal War, and I'd like to see the Operations version updated to match it. (Operations feels less responsive and more difficult to activate, while also being slower to recharge than its Eternal War counterpart.)
Menu navigation is inconsistent while using a controller, some menus I can navigate with the directional pad, and some menus require me to use the control sticks. Can feel a little clunky, but not that important in the long run.
